messages.author: 2c9138e143a7fe19
messages.subject: TIME FOR EXECUTING lavTestScore
parts:
I'm trying to run the following model
model_09="USELESS =~ qc8_1+qc8_3+qc8_4+qc8_5
  DISTRUST =~ qa3_1+qa3_2+qa3_3+qa3_4+qa3_5+qa3_6
  POPU =~ qa8_5+qa6a+d73_1_r";
hesit_ctry_config_9=cfa(model_09,orthogonal=FALSE, data=data_2, estimator="WLSMV", group="ctry_r",ordered=TRUE);
hesit_ctry_metric_9=cfa(model_09,orthogonal=FALSE, data=data_2, estimator="WLSMV", group="ctry_r", group.equal=c('loadings'),ordered=TRUE);
hesit_ctry_scalar_9=cfa(model_09,orthogonal=FALSE, data=data_2, estimator="WLSMV", group="ctry_r", group.equal=c('loadings', 'intercepts'),ordered=TRUE);

I have 28.000 cases in 28 countries.

Scalar invariance does not hold. I'm trying to run lavTestScore to view which fixed (or constrained) parameters in the model should be released to improve the fit for the scalar model.

It began two days ago and I'm wondering how much time I have to be waiting for obtaining the output. Is there any way to calculate it in advance? 

Thanks.

Manuel Recio-Menéndez

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: TIME FOR EXECUTING lavTestScore
parts: Scalar invariance does not hold.

You cannot conclude that without first constraining thresholds to equality.  Your loadings are not comparable if the scales of the latent response variables are not linked (by equating thresholds).  Try using semTools::measEq.syntax(), and reading the references on that help page.


I'm trying to run lavTestScore ... It began two days ago

That should not happen.  It should only take moments.
Is there any way to calculate it in advance?

In advance of what?  It is calculated from the first and second derivatives of the estimated model parameters, so you need to estimate a model first.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: TIME FOR EXECUTING lavTestScore
parts: you might be able to reduce the computation time if you apply the release argument: https://rdrr.io/cran/lavaan/man/lavTestScore.html

Indeed, I would be very specific about which constraints you want to test, so that those are the only calculations that occur.  Also, you could set univariate=FALSE to only obtain the combined test, and run lavTestScore() for one item at a time (i.e., releasing 6 constraints that make the other groups' parameters equal to the first group's for that item).  Hopefully that will make the computations less demanding for your very large model.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
